newsitem.title: USA: ITT seeks bids for top properties - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: ITT seeks bids for top properties - WSJ.

text.p: ITT Corp is considering bids to sell some of its premier properties under the condition that Hilton Hotels Corp, which has launched a takeover bid, would be barred from owning or managing them, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Tuesday's electronic edition, the Journal said ITT's move to sell such properties as the Italian Ciga hotels, the landmark St. Regis in New York and the Phoenician resort in Scottsdale, Ariz., could prove pivotal in its effort to fend off Hilton's $6.5 billion takeover bid.

Hilton president and chief executive Stephen Bollenbach said that if ITT sells a substantial number of its prime hotels under those conditions, it "would be a very effective way" of discouraging Hilton's bid. "The more they sell off the assets we want, the less interested we become."
Under the move, ITT is requiring purchasers of the properties to sign management contracts with ITT.
Last month, it agreed to sell five Sheraton hotels in the U.S. under similar terms to Felcore Suites Hotels Inc for $200 million.
On Monday, Bollenbach wrote a letter to ITT's board of directors, saying Hilton was ready to acquire the five ITT Sheraton hotels at the same price, but excluding the change-of-control provisions.
